description: Single-panel bar chart (no sub-panels) with a vertical gradient background from light blue at the top to pale orange at the bottom. The y-axis is labelled "Corrosion rate (mm/y)" and runs from 0.0 to 0.5 in major ticks of 0.1 with minor ticks; the x-axis is labelled "Samples" and carries four purple/violet bars with black error bars, in the order S0, S950, S1050, S1150. Each bar is annotated with its value printed above it: S0 = 0.326, S950 = 0.160, S1050 = 0.248, S1150 = 0.281. The bars are drawn thin and equal width. The visible trend is a maximum for S0, a minimum for S950, and a monotonic increase from S950 through S1050 to S1150, i.e. a V-shaped ranking. The error bars are small relative to the bar heights, consistent with the caption's reproducibility claim. The figure therefore demonstrates that solution treatment lowers the corrosion rate relative to the as-received S0 state, that the best corrosion resistance is obtained at 950 °C, and that higher solution-treatment temperatures progressively degrade that resistance. No grain-size values, test durations or electrolyte details are printed on the panel itself; the caption supplies the 30 d immersion in 3.5 wt% NaCl.

observations.observation: The bar chart plots corrosion rate on an axis labelled 'Corrosion rate (mm/y)' spanning 0.0 to 0.5 with 0.1 major-tick intervals.
Four samples are plotted in the order S0, S950, S1050, S1150 on an axis labelled 'Samples'.
The value printed above the S0 bar is 0.326 mm/y, the highest of the four bars.
The value printed above the S950 bar is 0.160 mm/y, the lowest of the four bars.
The printed values for S1050 and S1150 are 0.248 mm/y and 0.281 mm/y respectively, both higher than S950 but lower than S0.
Every bar carries a black error bar; the error bars are visibly small compared with the bar heights.
The caption states the corrosion rates were measured after immersion for 30 d in 3.5 wt% NaCl solution.
The citing text states the S0 sample has the highest corrosion rate (0.326 mm/y), reflecting its inferior corrosion resistance.
The citing text states the S950 sample exhibits the lowest corrosion rate at 0.160 mm/y and that the optimal corrosion resistance is achieved at 950 °C.
The citing text states the corrosion rates of S1050 and S1150 are 0.248 mm/y and 0.281 mm/y, and that as grain size increases the corrosion rate correspondingly increases.
The citing text claims experimental reproducibility with variations maintained below 3 % across multiple tests — a figure not printed anywhere on the panel.
The citing text links the corrosion-rate trend to grain size and to the Al content in the oxide film, and states it is consistent with Figs. 6 and 8.

subfigures.description: Bar chart of corrosion rate (mm/y) for four samples S0, S950, S1050 and S1150, with values printed above each bar (0.326, 0.160, 0.248, 0.281) and small black error bars; y-axis 0.0-0.5 mm/y, x-axis labelled Samples.
